task_title: timeout-kill assertions not stress-resilient under cap and network cut
task_criteria:
timeout-kill assertions are stress-resilient against a slow reaper: the two flaky entry points are boardbridge TestTimeoutKillsProcessGroup (internal/boardbridge/bridge_test.go:147) and harness TestAdapterContract/{pi,codex}/DeliverTimeoutKillsProcessGroup (internal/harness/contract_test.go:277). Three claims.
(A) the aliveness decision no longer accepts only ESRCH: waitDead accepts state Z or os.ErrNotExist with a bounded budget and names the observed state, stat error and budget when it fails (internal/harness/contract_test.go:976-988 using procState at contract_test.go:990), and the boardbridge equivalent counts a process-group member as live only when state != 'Z' (internal/boardbridge/bridge_test.go:181 waitProcessGroupDead, 195 liveProcessGroupMembers, 213 the Z test), reporting members plus stat_error (bridge_test.go:192).
(B) the pid evidence wait is bounded and loud: pidsWaitBound = 5*time.Second (contract_test.go:911) and readPIDs (contract_test.go:919) fails quoting the bound and the last on-disk content instead of reading a partial file.
(C) the clean and stressed legs agree and the gaps are named, not passed: .coding-hermes/evidence/QA-CRIER-60.md records base 7458b4d1 NOT red under MemoryMax=3G (ok 5.017s boardbridge / ok 0.836s harness), merged edab98f8 green on both legs, and lists the network-cut leg as an explicit named gap because this host cannot create a netns.
PROOF: go test -count=1 -run TestTimeoutKillsProcessGroup ./internal/boardbridge/ && sed -n '1,60p' .coding-hermes/evidence/QA-CRIER-60.md
FAILIF: an aliveness check still treats only ESRCH as death, an unbounded sleep decides aliveness, the failure text omits the observed state or budget, or the evidence file's named gaps are reported as passes.

items.detail: (A) internal/harness/contract_test.go:976-988 waitDead polls procState (defined :990) and returns only on `errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) || (err == nil && state == 'Z')`; the failure text at :987 is `pid %d is still live after the timeout kill — state=%q stat_error=%v budget=%s`, i.e. state + stat error + budget. boardbridge: bridge_test.go:181 waitProcessGroupDead, :195 liveProcessGroupMembers, :213 `if group == pgid && state != 'Z'`, :192 `t.Fatalf("process group %d still has live members after timeout kill: members=%v stat_error=%v", ...)`. No ESRCH-based aliveness remains in either test file — `grep -rn 'processAlive|syscall.Kill|syscall.ESRCH' internal/boardbridge/ internal/harness/` returns only production kill paths (internal/harness/exec_unix.go:25, internal/boardbridge/bridge.go:200), not assertions. (B) contract_test.go:911 `pidsWaitBound = 5 * time.Second`; :919 readPIDs loops to `deadline := time.Now().Add(pidsWaitBound)` and only returns when `len(pids) >= pidsWanted`; failures at :941 (`read pids: %v (waited %s for %s to hold %d pids)`) and :943 (`... within %s: %q`, lastRaw) quote the bound and the last on-disk content. (C) .coding-hermes/evidence/QA-CRIER-60.md:39-42 records base 7458b4d1 `ok 5.017s — FAILURE NOT REPRODUCED` (boardbridge) and `ok 0.836s — FAILURE NOT REPRODUCED` (harness), merged edab98f8 `ok 5.067s` / `ok 7.853s`; :50-52 records the network-cut leg as an explicit named gap ("this host cannot create a network namespace ... Recorded as a named gap, not a pass"). Tests run fresh: `go test -count=1 -run TestTimeoutKillsProcessGroup ./internal/boardbridge/` -> `ok github.com/crier-dev/crier/internal/boardbridge 5.073s` (exit 0); `go test -count=1 -run 'TestAdapterContract/(pi|codex)/DeliverTimeoutKillsProcessGroup' ./internal/harness/` -> `ok ... 0.821s` (exit 0); `go test -short -count=1 ./internal/boardbridge/ ./internal/harness/` -> `ok 6.097s` / `ok 8.789s`; `go vet ./internal/boardbridge/ ./internal/harness/` exit 0. [resolution 0.10; internal/boardbridge/bridge_test.go:147, internal/harness/contract_test.go:277, contract_test.go:990, bridge_test.go:192, .coding-hermes/evidence/QA-CRIER-60.md]

items.criterion: The new aliveness helpers are actually reached by the two named entry points: TestTimeoutKillsProcessGroup calls waitProcessGroupDead (bridge_test.go:175) and TestAdapterContract/{pi,codex}/DeliverTimeoutKillsProcessGroup calls readPIDs + waitDead (contract_test.go:457,462), so the zombie-aware decision is on the live path, not dead code.
items.detail: bridge_test.go:175 `waitProcessGroupDead(t, pid, 5*time.Second)` is the last statement of TestTimeoutKillsProcessGroup; contract_test.go:457 `pids := readPIDs(t, filepath.Join(f.dir, "pids"))` and :462 `waitDead(t, pid, 5*time.Second)` sit inside the `t.Run("DeliverTimeoutKillsProcessGroup", ...)` subtest at :441. `grep -rn 'waitProcessGroupDead|liveProcessGroupMembers|readProcStat' internal/` shows the only call sites are these, and the harness subtest run above (`ok ... 0.821s`) exercises them.

items.criterion: A genuinely live process still fails loudly: waitDead only returns on ErrNotExist or state=='Z' (contract_test.go:981), otherwise t.Fatalf at :987; waitProcessGroupDead only returns when len(members)==0 with err==nil (bridge_test.go:186), otherwise t.Fatalf at :192. A live (state R/S) member is counted by liveProcessGroupMembers (bridge_test.go:213) so the assertion cannot pass on a surviving process.
items.detail: contract_test.go:981 `if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) || (err == nil && state == 'Z') { return }` — every other outcome (live state, EPERM, malformed stat) falls through to `t.Fatalf` at :987. bridge_test.go:186 `if err == nil && len(members) == 0 { return }` — a non-Z member keeps the loop running and ends in `t.Fatalf` at :192; :213 `if group == pgid && state != 'Z'` is what puts a live member in the list. The change therefore only reclassifies zombies/absent pids as dead, not live processes.

items.criterion: The evidence file's claimed base/merged results are consistent with what the tree actually contains (the pre-fix code at base 7458b4d1 really did use syscall.Kill/ESRCH, and the merged tree really has the zombie-aware helpers), so the recorded runs are not fabricated against a different tree.
items.detail: `git cat-file -t 7458b4d1` -> commit and `git cat-file -t edab98f8` -> commit (both present). `git show 7458b4d1:internal/boardbridge/bridge_test.go` shows `err = syscall.Kill(-pid, 0)` / `if errors.Is(err, syscall.ESRCH)` and `git show 7458b4d1:internal/harness/contract_test.go` shows `processAlive` at :1062 with `err := syscall.Kill(pid, 0)` at :1063 — exactly the mechanism the evidence file quotes at lines 13-14. HEAD (merged) contains the zombie-aware helpers (commit 05f5e1bc, `git show 05f5e1bc --stat`: bridge_test.go +71/-…, contract_test.go +34/-…).

(A) the aliveness decision no longer accepts only ESRCH: waitDead accepts state Z or os.ErrNotExist with a bounded budget and names the observed state, stat error and budget when it fails (internal/harness/contract_test.go:976-988 using procState at contract_test.go:990), and the boardbridge equivalent counts a process-group member as live only when state != 'Z' (internal/boardbridge/bridge_test.go:181 waitProcessGroupDead, 195 liveProcessGroupMembers, 213 the Z test), reporting members plus stat_error (bridge_test.go:192).
(B) the pid evidence wait is bounded and loud: pidsWaitBound = 5*time.Second (contract_test.go:911) and readPIDs (contract_test.go:919) fails quoting the bound and the last on-disk content instead of reading a partial file.
(C) the clean and stressed legs agree and the gaps are named, not passed: .coding-hermes/evidence/QA-CRIER-60.md records base 7458b4d1 NOT red under MemoryMax=3G (ok 5.017s boardbridge / ok 0.836s harness), merged edab98f8 green on both legs, and lists the network-cut leg as an explicit named gap because this host cannot create a netns.

FAILIF: an aliveness check still treats only ESRCH as death, an unbounded sleep decides aliveness, the failure text omits the observed state or budget, or the evidence file's named gaps are reported as passes.: (A) internal/harness/contract_test.go:976-988 waitDead polls procState (defined :990) and returns only on `errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) || (err == nil && state == 'Z')`; the failure text at :987 is `pid %d is still live after the timeout kill — state=%q stat_error=%v budget=%s`, i.e. state + stat error + budget. boardbridge: bridge_test.go:181 waitProcessGroupDead, :195 liveProcessGroupMembers, :213 `if group == pgid && state != 'Z'`, :192 `t.Fatalf("process group %d still has live members after timeout kill: members=%v stat_error=%v", ...)`. No ESRCH-based aliveness remains in either test file — `grep -rn 'processAlive|syscall.Kill|syscall.ESRCH' internal/boardbridge/ internal/harness/` returns only production kill paths (internal/harness/exec_unix.go:25, internal/boardbridge/bridge.go:200), not assertions. (B) contract_test.go:911 `pidsWaitBound = 5 * time.Second`; :919 readPIDs loops to `deadline := time.Now().Add(pidsWaitBound)` and only returns when `len(pids) >= pidsWanted`; failures at :941 (`read pids: %v (waited %s for %s to hold %d pids)`) and :943 (`... within %s: %q`, lastRaw) quote the bound and the last on-disk content.   ✓ A genuinely live process still fails loudly: waitDead only returns on ErrNotExist or state=='Z' (contract_test.go:981), otherwise t.Fatalf at :987; waitProcessGroupDead only returns when len(members)==0 with err==nil (bridge_test.go:186), otherwise t.Fatalf at :192. A live (state R/S) member is counted by liveProcessGroupMembers (bridge_test.go:213) so the assertion cannot pass on a surviving process.: contract_test.go:981 `if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) || (err == nil && state == 'Z') { return }` — every other outcome (live state, EPERM, malformed stat) falls through to `t.Fatalf` at :987. bridge_test.go:186 `if err == nil && len(members) == 0 { return }` — a non-Z member keeps the loop running and ends in `t.Fatalf` at :192; :213 `if group == pgid && state != 'Z'` is what puts a live member in the list. The change therefore only reclassifies zombies/absent pids as dead, not live processes.
  ✓ The evidence file's claimed base/merged results are consistent with what the tree actually contains (the pre-fix code at base 7458b4d1 really did use syscall.Kill/ESRCH, and the merged tree really has the zombie-aware helpers), so the recorded runs are not fabricated against a different tree.: `git cat-file -t 7458b4d1` -> commit and `git cat-file -t edab98f8` -> commit (both present). `git show 7458b4d1:internal/boardbridge/bridge_test.go` shows `err = syscall.Kill(-pid, 0)` / `if errors.Is(err, syscall.ESRCH)` and `git show 7458b4d1:internal/harness/contract_test.go` shows `processAlive` at :1062 with `err := syscall.Kill(pid, 0)` at :1063 — exactly the mechanism the evidence file quotes at lines 13-14. HEAD (merged) contains the zombie-aware helpers (commit 05f5e1bc, `git show 05f5e1bc --stat`: bridge_test.go +71/-…, contract_test.go +34/-…).
Both flaky entry points now decide aliveness from /proc state (Z or ErrNotExist) with bounded, loud budgets, readPIDs is bounded and quotes the bound plus last on-disk content, and the evidence file records the base/merged runs honestly with the network-cut leg named as a gap rather than a pass; the named tests pass fresh (ok 5.073s boardbridge, ok 0.821s harness).
